headline: High: xonsh can read/write and exfiltrate shared files while LightZero is non-interactive, creating data-leak and workflow-conflict risk; prompt-injection risk is low because LightZero has no input channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero has no filesystem, shell, MCP, or browser surfaces, so it cannot ingest xonsh output by default. xonsh can read/write files and process stdin/stdout, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or an external workspace, so injection is possible but limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies xonsh output into LightZero prompts or configs, injection becomes plausible.
IF both agents are connected through a shared file or message channel, LightZero could ingest attacker-controlled content.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of untrusted xonsh output into LightZero inputs.
Use a review step before any file produced by xonsh is consumed by LightZero.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to files passed between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: xonsh can read filesystem contents and has broad network egress, while LightZero has no filesystem access or egress. If they share a workspace, xonsh can expose files that LightZero would otherwise not touch, and xonsh can transmit them off-host. The pairwise leak path is therefore real in common setups, though not proven by direct interaction evidence.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory, xonsh can read files that LightZero cannot.
IF xonsh is allowed to reach the network, any file it reads can be exfiltrated.
IF LightZero outputs are written to disk and then consumed by xonsh, those outputs can be leaked.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Restrict xonsh network egress during shared tasks.
Avoid placing secrets in any shared workspace.
Review file permissions before starting both agents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent sandboxing and network policy.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero cannot write files or modify git state, but xonsh can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses. If both are aimed at the same mutable workspace, xonsh can overwrite artifacts that LightZero reads or produces, creating a write/read conflict even though LightZero itself is non-writing. Uncertainty about the orchestrator means the safer medium choice applies.
conditions: IF both agents share a writable directory, xonsh can overwrite LightZero artifacts.
IF the orchestrator lacks locking, concurrent edits can race.
IF xonsh writes generated code or configs into the same path LightZero reads, conflicts occur.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Run only one writer at a time.
Turn on file locking in the orchestrator.
Check git status before and after xonsh runs.
requires-engineering: add workspace-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightZero is a game-playing system with no action-taking authority, while xonsh can execute shell commands and manipulate files. If xonsh consumes LightZero outputs as authoritative, it may act on incorrect game-state or generated artifacts without verification. The blast radius is limited to workflow errors, but the pathway exists in default file-based integrations.
conditions: IF xonsh treats LightZero output files as trusted inputs, errors can cascade.
IF LightZero-generated text is piped into shell commands, xonsh may execute bad actions.
IF no validation step exists between the agents, incorrect outputs propagate.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before xonsh acts on LightZero output.
Validate file formats before execution.
Use read-only handoff files.
Log and diff all generated artifacts.
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data classes, residency constraints, or regulated permissions are documented for either agent. LightZero touches no data classes and xonsh lists general engineering artifacts only, so there is no evidenced residency or certification mismatch to assess.
conditions: IF either agent is later configured to process regulated data, reassess compliance.
IF a deployment adds residency or retention requirements, the current profiles are insufficient.
mitigations: Document any regulated data flows before deployment.
Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Review retention settings if new data classes are added.
